message.content:
Based on my search, here's how to log in to your **My Service Canada Account (MSCA)**:

## Official Login Page

Go to the official Government of Canada portal:
**https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/my-account.html**

## Sign-In Options

You have **three ways** to log in:

| Method | What You Need |
|--------|---------------|
| **GCKey** | A Government of Canada username and password (works across multiple government services) |
| **Sign-In Partner** | Your existing online banking credentials from participating banks (RBC, TD, Scotiabank, BMO, CIBC, National Bank, Desjardins, etc.) |
| **Provincial Digital ID** | Available if you live in **Alberta** or **British Columbia** |

## Step-by-Step Login Process

1. **Visit** the official MSCA login page
2. **Select your sign-in method** (GCKey, Sign-In Partner, or Provincial ID)
3. **Enter your credentials** (username/password or banking login)
4. **Complete identity validation** if prompted (may include answering security questions)
5. **Access your dashboard** to manage benefits

## What You Can Access in MSCA

- Employment Insurance (EI) claims and reports
- Canada Pension Plan (CPP) benefits and contributions
- Old Age Security (OAS) and Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS)
- Social Insurance Number (SIN) information
- Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP)
- Direct deposit and personal information updates
- Tax slips (T4E, T4A)

## Important Notes

- **First-time users**: You may need to register and verify your identity. A **Personal Access Code (PAC)** may be mailed to you (takes 5-10 business days)
- **GCKey is NOT the same as CRA login** — they are separate systems
- **Need help?** Contact Service Canada at **1-800-O-Canada (1-800-622-6232)**

## If You Access Student Loans

As of **May 25, 2025**, the National Student Loans Service Centre (NSLSC) now uses MSCA as its login portal. You can no longer use old NSLSC credentials directly.
